title: AmberWave partner scouting notes
content:
Quick personal notes for AmberWave outreach / scouting.

Account snapshot:
- Company: AmberWave (fintech: consumer payments + rewards). HQ: Denver. ~350 employees, Series B (2023).
- Tech footprint: uses AWS predominantly, some GCP for analytics. In-house ML team (2 senior ML infra, 3 ML engineers), product teams focused on chatbots + customer support.
- Signals: job postings for "ML infra engineer" + "real-time personalization" in last 6 months. Recent blog post about latency problems in recommendation engine.
- Likely infra: Kubernetes + managed GPUs for training, but serving is mostly CPU-based microservices.

Why Redwood might matter to them (top-line):
- They need lower-latency real-time prompts for in-prod chat ranking & personalized responses (current infra too slow, mentions 400-600ms p95).
- Cost pressure: token-level costs spiking for high volume support flows.
- Security/compliance: dealing with PII in chat transcripts — potential interest in Private deployment or Dedicated.
- Scale: mid-market -> enterprise scaling challenge; they'd value predictable capacity and rollout controls.

Primary stakeholders to target (names TBD):
- CTO or Head of Platform (platform + infra budget)
- Head of ML / ML Infra Lead (technical decision maker)
- Head of Customer Support Product (product owner for observability/quality)
- Security/Compliance Manager (if we get over security objections)

High-level positioning for outreach:
- Emphasize: predictable latency SLOs, cost controls (batching + quantization recs), private/dedicated options for data isolation, easy migration with same API.
- 1-sentence pitch: "We help teams drop 2–5x inference cost and shave 100–300ms off p95 for real-time chat without changing the product API — can we share a short performance plan?"

Cold email subject lines (A/B ideas):
- "Cut AmberWave's chat latency by 100–300ms (quick plan)"
- "Proof: 2–4x lower token cost for real-time support flows"
- "Private inference + SLAs for PII-sensitive chat — short note"

Draft email (short):
Hi <FirstName>,

Saw AmberWave's notes on improving personalization latency — quick intro: I'm Maya on the Redwood Inference outreach team. We work with mid-market fintechs to get predictable low-latency inference while reducing per-token cost.

In similar setups we've:
- Reduced p95 for chat / reranking by ~120–300ms,
- Cut token costs 2–3x with batching + quantization, and
- Certified private deployments for PII-sensitive workloads.

Would love to share a 1-page plan tuned to your stack and a 2-week pilot approach. Are you the right person to connect, or who should I speak with?

Thanks,
Maya

LinkedIn message (short):
Hi <Name> — noticed AmberWave is hiring ML infra engineers. I help teams improve real-time inference latency + cost without rewriting product code. Quick chat next week?

Phone / discovery script (30–60s):
- Intro: Maya, Redwood Inference — helping products put low-latency LLMs into production.
- Problem check: I read your blog about recommendation latency — are you seeing slowdowns when the model scales? How much is p95 now?
- Value: We can usually cut tail latency and unit costs; we also offer private deployments for PII.
- Ask: Can I put together a lightweight performance plan for your stack?

Key technical questions to surface in a discovery call:
- Current inference stack: self-hosted, cloud-managed, or mixed? GPUs?
- Models in use: Open-source LLMs (which families), quantized?
- Typical sequence lengths and concurrency for chat flows? p50/p95 latency targets?
- Data sensitivity: PII/PCI/PHI? Any compliance needs (SOC2, ISO)?
- Release cadence and who owns rollout decisions?

Objection handling (draft)
- "We host our own models / built infra":
  - Short: Great — many customers start there. We can work as a drop-in inference runtime or provide dedicated pods to reduce tail latency and improve kernel selection without migrating training pipelines.
  - Detail: emphasize same API surface, non-invasive KV cache and batching layers.
- "Security / compliance concerns":
  - Short: We support Private deployments + KMS integrations and give audit logs; can run in your VPC or air-gapped on prem for enterprise contracts.
- "Cost / vendor lock":
  - Short: PoC focused on measurable unit economics (per-token cost) and fallback policies. Start small (2-week pilot) and measure.
- "We are already on Provider X's managed endpoints":
  - Short: We compare actual token and latency metrics vs provider-managed endpoints and often show better economics at scale due to batching, caching, and low-level kernel optimizations.

Pilot / PoC playbook (2-week light template):
- Week 0 (prep): NDA as needed, access to a representative prompt set, small telemetry sample (logs).
- Week 1: Run parallel inference against current endpoint + Redwood test harness (metrics: p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost estimate). Quick tuning: batching, quant profiles.
- Week 2: Deliver report + recommended config (quant + routing + cache) and proposal for Dedicated/Private deployment if gains look good.
- Success criteria: 15–25% cost reduction OR 100–200ms p95 improvement for pilot traffic; agreement on next steps.

Personal TODOs / next actions:
- Find AmberWave ML infra lead name (search LinkedIn + recent blog authors) — assigned Jared.
- Pull any public blog posts and craft a 1-page plan (Samira to draft initial metrics table).
- Attach quick benchmark sketch comparing typical AWS endpoint -> Redwood Dedicated for mid-market chat (use RD-1423 benchmark as reference).
- Send first outbound email to CTO + follow-up via LinkedIn in 3 days.

Notes to self (random thoughts):
- Might be good to call out "canary rollouts + automatic fallback" as a selling point — ops teams worry about model regressions.
- If they care about inference cost, show a sample ROI spreadsheet: current monthly token spend vs projected after batching + quant. Quick numbers look persuasive.
- Prepare 1 slide with architecture diagram for Private deploy (control plane vs customer-managed dataplane) — non-technical execs like visuals.

Possible red flags to watch during outreach:
- Strong internal preference for one cloud provider that restricts external runtimes.
- No clear ownership of model serving (diffused responsibility).
- Procurement timeline >6 months (low near-term opportunity).

Meeting prep checklist (if intro accepted):
- Bring short demo or recorded benchmark (30s video + 1 slide of results).
- Have questions ready about retention/telemetry needs and KPI owners.
- Decide who from Redwood (solutions eng + product) should join — likely include solutions eng for technical deep-dive.

End of notes.

-- Maya
